summary: CCC-built C-3 cab lookout on a steel tower in Sierra National Forest, Fresno County; NHLR-registered 1999 and still in service per NHLR. Build year and height differ between sources.

facts.design: C-3 wooden cab (14 by 14 ft) with catwalk on a 30-32 ft K-braced steel tower with straight stairway

access.note: Seasonal: closed in winter due to heavy snow; in summer the public may access the tower and surrounding area when open for service (fire-lookouts.org, older page)

visit.trail_note: Closed in winter due to heavy snow. Sources read give no drive-up or trail directions and do not say whether the cab may be climbed.

events.note: Built by the CCC as a compass lookout with steel structure base; fire-lookouts.org gives 1934. Forest Lookouts gives 1935 (see resolved_conflicts)
Maintenance by volunteers over several weekends: new cabinets, new floor, plumbing upgrades (FFLA report as reproduced on fire-lookouts.org)
New roof and outhouse scheduled; completion not confirmed in sources read

corrections.why: 18.3 m is about 60 ft, which neither source gives for the tower; the record's own design line says 30-ft tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: fire-lookouts.org says 1934 and NHLR says only that it was CCC-built; Forest Lookouts says 1935. The story uses 1934 and notes the 1935 figure.
NHLR gives a 30-32 ft tower; fire-lookouts.org gives 34 ft. No height_m fact is set because the sources disagree.
NHLR gives 9,026 ft (2,751 m); fire-lookouts.org gives 9,018 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.
fire-lookouts.org gives 37.2235 N, 119.1048 W, about 18 km from the NHLR coordinates used in the record. The record keeps the NHLR coordinates; the difference is unresolved.

sources.title: Mount Tom Fire Lookout, A United States Forest Service Lookout

notes_for_editor: Core facts (USFS administration, CCC origin, C-3 cab, 1999 NHLR registration, still in service per NHLR) are solid across the NHLR page and fire-lookouts.org. Build year (1934 vs 1935), height (30-32 ft vs 34 ft), elevation and coordinates disagree between sources; the record's 18.3 m height is not supported by either and is proposed for correction. Not verified: the brief's 2010 'Fresno County RAC grant' and 2011 RAC grant (about $18,000), and the 2018 FFLA restoration grant. The FFLA 2018 PDF (firelookout.org cr-ca-sierra-2018.pdf) returned no readable text, and no readable source mentions the RAC grants, so these are left out of events. 'BRF' in the 2010 report is not expanded in any source read. Staffing, notable fires and rental status were not found. A WebSearch snippet from fs.usda.gov (media/135997) says Mount Tom is the only Sierra NF lookout eligible for NRHP listing, but that PDF returned no text in fetch and is not cited. Also unread: onX and peakbagging.com pages (snippets give 30-34 ft and 9,030 ft). Current access should be checked with the Sierra National Forest before trusting the seasonal access note.
